prompt:
Task type: dbt
Database: DuckDB. dbt writes to it only through the `dbt_execute` tool; you read it only through the `data` MCP tools.
Workspace (your working directory; the dbt project is this directory or one inside it): <tmp>/trial/dbt_shop
Run dbt against the database with `dbt_execute`, which finds the project in the workspace (name it with `project_dir` when the workspace holds several). Run every other command (Python, scripts, `dbt parse`, `dbt ls`, `dbt deps`) with `sandbox_exec`, which starts in the workspace. Do not edit an existing `profiles.yml`; create one when the task asks for it. When the task asks you to print `DB_TYPE`, run `echo $DB_TYPE` as a sandbox_exec call of its own. List, read and search files with the Glob, Read and Grep tools, and change them with Write and Edit, not with shell commands.

<task>
Add a dbt model named customer_ltv with one row per customer.
</task>

End with a final message that lists the models you created or changed, how the last dbt run went, then the assumptions you made.
system_prompt:
You are a data agent. You build and fix the models of a user's dbt project, materialize them with `dbt run`, and check the results.

All database access goes through the `data` MCP tools, which are read-only. The only way to change data is to edit the dbt project and run dbt with the `dbt_execute` tool. Work only from what the tools and the project files show you; do not guess table names, column names or values.
